### OBL-024 — AI risk management before any AI feature

| Field              | Value                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | NIST (SRC-033)                                                                                |
| Authority type     | voluntary-framework                                                                           |
| Citation           | NIST AI 100-1                                                                                 |
| Locator            | https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10 |
| Source version     | 1.0                                                                                           |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                    |
| Jurisdiction       | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL                                                                            |
| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                                                   |
| Trigger            | An AI feature is proposed for SSLS.                                                           |
| Control family     | AI GOVERNANCE                                                                                 |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                                                |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                                                  |
| Owning route       | Gate condition on any AI capability                                                           |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                                                 |
| Review trigger     | Any proposed AI capability                                                                    |

**What the source states.** NIST states the framework is voluntary. A revision is in progress.

**Obligation.** Voluntary process guidance for governing, mapping, measuring and managing AI risks. It is neither mandatory nor certifiable.

**SSLS interpretation.** The existing value-stream AI gating rules are the placeholder for this. They are refusal rules, not a risk-management program.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. The program prohibits AI features in the current phase.

**Future phase.** A govern, map, measure and manage cycle would need to exist before, not after, a first AI feature.

**Required control.** An AI risk process bound to a gate that precedes any model integration.

**Current control.** Prohibition. AI features are refused in the current phase and the refusal is encoded in the value-stream gates.

**Evidence required.** Risk process artifact plus per-feature records. Minimum method: Reviewed documentation.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it has no AI features.

**Claim refused.** NIST AI RMF aligned; responsible AI certified

**Note.** NIST AI 600-1 and ISO/IEC 42001 travel with this obligation as reference sources.

### OBL-025 — Existing law applies to AI claims and behaviour

| Field              | Value                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General (SRC-014)                                              |
| Authority type     | official-guidance                                                                                   |
| Citation           | AGO AI Advisory, 2024-04-16                                                                         |
| Locator            | https://www.mass.gov/doc/ago-ai-advisory-41624/download                                             |
| Source version     | 2024-04-16                                                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                          |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                                                               |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-NOW                                                                                         |
| Trigger            | SSLS makes any public statement about AI capability, including a statement about future capability. |
| Control family     | CLAIMS / TRANSPARENCY                                                                               |
| Control status     | IMPLEMENTED                                                                                         |
| Evidence status    | CURRENT                                                                                             |
| Owning route       | Maintained across all work packages; established in WP-000                                          |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                                                       |
| Review trigger     | Every published change to a public surface                                                          |

**What the source states.** The Attorney General states how existing law applies. The advisory is guidance interpreting statutes such as c. 93A.

**Obligation.** Existing Massachusetts consumer protection, anti-discrimination and data security law applies to developers, suppliers and users of AI, and the advisory creates no new AI-specific statute.

**SSLS interpretation.** Claim discipline is a legal control, not a style preference. The Claims Register is the operating control for this obligation.

**Current phase.** Applies now to marketing and public-surface language even though no AI feature exists.

**Future phase.** Applies with greater force once any AI feature ships.

**Required control.** A maintained claims register with prohibited wording, applied to every public surface.

**Current control.** Claims Register CLM-001 to CLM-013 with recorded prohibited claims, plus a refused-claims boundary surface in the application.

**Evidence required.** The register plus review of published surfaces against it. Minimum method: Reviewed register with per-surface check.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it maintains a claims register and refuses specified claims.

**Claim refused.** AI-powered; AI-driven insights; intelligent recommendations

**Note.** This is one of the few obligations that applies right now to the current build.

### OBL-026 — Developer-directed AI design expectations

| Field              | Value                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Education, Office of Educational Technology (SRC-036) |
| Authority type     | official-guidance                                                        |
| Citation           | Designing for Education with AI: An Essential Guide for Developers       |
| Locator            | https://www.ed.gov/sites/ed/files/documents/ai-report/ai-report.pdf      |
| Source version     | 2023 report with 2024 developer guide                                    |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                               |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                               |
| Applicability      | REFERENCE                                                                |
| Trigger            | Any AI capability design.                                                |
| Control family     | HUMAN REVIEW                                                             |
| Control status     | SPECIFICATION-ONLY                                                       |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                             |
| Owning route       | Gate condition on any AI capability                                      |
| Review requirement | EDUCATION POLICY REVIEW REQUIRED                                         |
| Review trigger     | Any proposed AI capability                                               |

**What the source states.** The Department states the guidance is non-regulatory and that examples are not endorsements.

**Obligation.** Non-regulatory recommendations for developers on evidence, transparency, human oversight and equity in educational AI.

**SSLS interpretation.** Its emphasis on evidence-bound output and human review matches the SSLS rule that AI output must be reviewable and never autonomously decide.

**Current phase.** Reference. Explicitly non-regulatory.

**Future phase.** Would inform design review for any AI capability.

**Required control.** Human review requirement on any AI-produced output.

**Current control.** Encoded as a refusal rule: no autonomous high-impact decisions, and no AI features in this phase.

**Evidence required.** Design record per AI feature. Minimum method: Reviewed design record.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Department of Education endorsed; ED aligned

### OBL-027 — Colorado automated decision-making watch item

| Field              | Value                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Colorado General Assembly (SRC-037)                                                                                        |
| Authority type     | statute                                                                                                                    |
| Citation           | SB 26-189                                                                                                                  |
| Locator            | https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/SB26-189                                                                                    |
| Source version     | Signed 2026-05-14                                                                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                                                 |
| Jurisdiction       | US-STATE-OTHER                                                                                                             |
| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                                                                                |
| Trigger            | SSLS develops or deploys a high-risk automated decision-making system affecting Colorado residents on or after 2027-01-01. |
| Control family     | AI GOVERNANCE                                                                                                              |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                                                                             |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                                                                               |
| Owning route       | Watch item; re-check before 2027-01-01                                                                                     |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                                                      |
| Review trigger     | Any recommendation or eligibility-scoring capability, or Colorado market entry                                             |

**What the source states.** The bill text states the effective date. Its scope was narrowed relative to SB 24-205.

**Obligation.** Signed 2026-05-14, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act with a narrower framework effective 2027-01-01.

**SSLS interpretation.** Tracked because a governed learner-record product that recommended placement or eligibility could fall within a consequential-decision definition.

**Current phase.** Not applicable. The law is not yet effective and there is no Colorado presence or automated decision capability.

**Future phase.** Would impose developer and deployer duties including impact assessment and consumer disclosure.

**Required control.** None yet. A scope determination at the point any recommendation capability is proposed.

**Current control.** Not applicable. No automated decision capability exists.

**Evidence required.** Scope determination record if triggered. Minimum method: Reviewed determination with legal input.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Colorado AI Act compliant

**Note.** Recorded as ADOPTED-NOT-YET-EFFECTIVE at source level to prevent a present-tense obligation.
